stories.headline: NIA court frees 4 held for 2020 Srinagar terror attack that killed 2 soldiers
stories.title: NIA court frees 4 held for 2020 Srinagar terror attack that killed 2 soldiers
stories.summary: A special NIA court ruled that four men were not guilty of aiding terrorists in the 2020 attack. The prosecution could not establish any direct link between the men and the terrorists involved in the incident. Although two Army soldiers were killed, the evidence presented was circumstantial and insufficient. The court emphasized the necessity of legal proof despite the crime's severity and implications.

stories.headline: No Winter Session of Parliament? Skipped only four times in history
stories.title: No Winter Session of Parliament? Skipped only four times in history
stories.summary: Each previous instance coincided with extraordinary disruptions, from the Emergency and Lok Sabha dissolutions to Indira Gandhi’s assassination and the COVID-19 pandemic
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Winter Session of Parliament has been skipped only four times in India’s parliamentary history, and each instance was linked to exceptional circumstances, including the Emergency, the premature dissolution of the Lok Sabha, the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

With the Monsoon Session yet to be prorogued, setting a record for Parliament remaining unprorogued for more than 100 days, speculation has grown over the possibility of a short special session to consider the delimitation Bill.
The absence of any move to summon Parliament for its customary winter sitting has also fuelled discussion about whether the session could be skipped altogether.
The first time Parliament missed its winter session was during the 19-month Emergency.
The Lok Sabha met from July 21 to August 7, 1975, and then only from January 5 to February 6, 1976, without sitting during November or December, when the Winter Session is normally held.
The next instance came in 1979 after the premature dissolution of the Sixth Lok Sabha on August 22.
The newly elected House met only in January 1980, resulting in the Winter Session being skipped.
A similar situation arose in 1984 following the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on October 31.
General elections were called, and the Eighth Lok Sabha held its first sitting on January 15, 1985.
After a gap of 36 years, the Winter Session was skipped again in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Amid fears over the spread of the virus and stringent social-distancing norms, Parliament did not meet after the truncated Monsoon Session that ran from September 14 to 23.
In the 12 years of the Narendra Modi government, the timing of the Winter Session has varied considerably.
